correctness.rationale: For S=0,1,2,3 the nonnegative payoff discrepancy is zero at 0 and 3 and bounded by 3 alpha r theta (2/3)^gamma; all agents share that nonnegative interval, so an imitation payoff difference changes by at most its width. The Fermi logistic derivative is at most 1/4 and independent flip mutation multiplies probability differences by |1-2mu|. The resulting sharper one-row bound delta/2 implies the stated delta, T-step maximal coupling and KT bounds. With 0<mu<=1/2, Bernoulli KL<=chi-square, common (i,j) sampling, data processing and Markov KL chain rule prove KL<=KT(delta/2)^2/[mu(1-mu)], then Pinsker. Prescribing each focal exactly once and mutation to a specified target yields a valid N-step minorization epsilon=(2mu/N)^N and stationarity perturbation <=Ndelta/epsilon. The two-triad four-agent initial witness has a nonzero Bernoulli gap c(2/3)^gamma+o(...); K independent resets give matching exponent via midpoint testing. These are fixed-finite-N, fixed-sampling-kernel claims; no infinite-population phase transition or universal prefactor optimality is implied.

originality.rationale: Tang–Rao supply the two reward formulas and demonstrate qualitatively related simulated cooperative transitions; local convergence of the rewards is therefore not novel. Generic finite Markov coupling, KL, hypothesis-testing and Doeblin results are prior tools. The conjunction of explicit uniform gamma-dependence for this normalized Fermi-flip chain, a sharp exponential one-step witness, and a matching repeated-restart detection threshold was not found as a prior statement or immediate source-paper corollary. This is a best-of-knowledge specialist synthesis, not originality of generic perturbation theory.

A broader finite-chain statistical experiment comparison could imply this exact special case with different wording.
The stated sharpness concerns a resettable four-agent experiment, not arbitrary uncontrolled trajectories.

value.rationale: There is a mathematically motivated identifiability gap: simulations of two differently motivated higher-order game benefits may become hard to distinguish as curvature increases. Explicit trajectory, information and stationary bounds quantify that ambiguity on finite networks, and the restart witness identifies exactly which exponential observation budget can resolve it. That is more than a pointwise payoff limit, while remaining deliberately finite-population.
